questionText:
Match each addressing mode in List I with a data element or an element of a data structure (in a high-level language) in List II:

List IList II
P. Immediate1. Element of an array
Q. Indirect2. Pointer
R. Base with index3. Element of a record
S. Base with offset/displacement4. Constant
explanation:
Step 1: Match P (Immediate Addressing)
In Immediate Addressing, the value itself is provided inside the instruction. This corresponds to a Constant in high-level languages (P $\rightarrow$ 4).

Step 2: Match Q (Indirect Addressing)
In Indirect Addressing, the address of the operand is stored in a memory location/register. This corresponds to a Pointer dereference (Q $\rightarrow$ 2).

Step 3: Match R (Base with Index)
Base with Index addressing mode calculates the address as $\text{Base Address} + \text{Index}$, which is used to access an Element of an array where elements are indexed (R $\rightarrow$ 1).

Step 4: Match S (Base with offset/displacement)
Base with offset/displacement uses a fixed base pointer to the structure and an offset to access a specific field, representing an Element of a record or structure (S $\rightarrow$ 3).

Therefore, the correct matching is P–4, Q–2, R–1, S–3 (Option B).
